summary_paragraph: The patient, a morbidly obese male with a history of HLA-B27 positive ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, asthma, obstructive sleep apnea, and anxiety, was admitted for a severe flare of left hip and cervical spine pain, along with bilateral lower extremity edema. He reported difficulty with daily activities and developed transient dyspnea en route to the hospital. Evaluation revealed no evidence of infection, pulmonary embolism, or cardiac ischemia. Pain was managed with IV and oral opioids, NSAIDs, and a left hip joint injection with Marcaine and Kenalog under fluoroscopic guidance, which provided partial relief. Edema was attributed to venous insufficiency rather than cardiac or renal causes. The patient was stabilized, transitioned back to home medications, and discharged with follow-up plans in rheumatology, pain psychology, and primary care. He expressed interest in using medical marijuana to taper off opioids and was counseled on gradual weaning.
problems: Ankylosing spondylitis of unspecified sites in spine
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
